# Production ML at Scale: Distributed Training with PyTorch, Kubeflow, Spark & Feast on Red Hat OpenShift AI

## **🚀 Recommended Use Case: "Multimodal Customer Intelligence at Scale"**

**Multimodal Support & Personalization Engine**: this involves processing massive amounts of structured data (transactions) and unstructured data (support call transcripts/emails) to fine-tune a domain-specific model.

### **Why this fits:**

* **Scale:** Uses the **Amazon Customer Reviews Dataset** (5GB to 100GB+) or the **Common Crawl/Stack Exchange** datasets.  
* **GenAI/LLM:** Fine-tuning a **Llama 3** or **Mistral** model using **PyTorch FSDP** (Fully Sharded Data Parallel) for domain-specific sentiment and automated response generation.  
* **Feast:** Manages "Feature Store" entities like `customer_lifetime_value` or `recent_interaction_score` that are joined with LLM prompts at inference time to ground context using consistent feature serving (RAG-lite).  
* **Spark:** Handles the heavy lifting of tokenizing billions of words and cleaning tabular transaction data.  
* **Slurm/Kubeflow:** Slurm handles the "HPC-style" heavy fine-tuning on dedicated GPU nodes, while Kubeflow orchestrates the end-to-end pipeline.

### **📊 The Training Dataset**

The ideal candidate is the **Amazon Customer Reviews Dataset (2024-2026 Edition)** or the **Bitext E-commerce Support Dataset**.

For the LLM fine-tuning, we will use a **combined multimodal dataset**:

1. **Unstructured (The "Why"):** \~100GB+ of raw customer review text and support ticket transcripts (from the Amazon/Hugging Face datasets). This is what the LLM is fine-tuned on to learn the "company voice" and specific product nuances.  
2. **Structured (The "Context"):** Relational data like `user_id`, `purchase_history`, `loyalty_status`, and `shipping_region`. This data is **not** used to train the LLM directly; instead, it's processed by **Spark** and stored in **Feast** to be injected into the prompt during inference.

## **👤 The User Experience: "Hyper-Personalized Support"**

The "Magic" happens when a customer interacts with the fine-tuned model. Here is the lifecycle of a single user request:

### **1\. The Interaction**

A user types: *"I bought the wireless headphones last week and they won't charge. This is the third time I've had issues with this brand."*

### **2\. The Feature Fetch (Behind the Scenes)**

The application doesn't just send that text to the LLM. It hits the **Feast Online Store** using the User's ID.

* **Feast returns:** `Loyalty: Platinum`, `Total_Spent: $1,200`, `Last_3_Sentiment: Negative`.

### **3\. Contextual Prompt Injection**

The system wraps the user's complaint with the Feast data:

**System Prompt:** "You are a senior support agent. A **Platinum** customer (High Value) is frustrated after **three consecutive negative experiences**. Use a highly apologetic tone and prioritize a refund or replacement." **User Input:** "...headphones won't charge..."

### **4\. The Result**

The user receives a response like: *"As one of our Platinum members, we truly value your loyalty, and I am incredibly sorry this is your third poor experience. I've already initiated a full refund for your headphones and a 20% discount code for your next order."*

## **🛠️ Components Mapping**

| Component | Technical Role in Demo |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Spark** | Distributed Tokenization & Tabular Feature Engineering.Optional [RAPIDS Accelerator for Apache Spark](https://nvidia.github.io/spark-rapids/). |
| **Feast** | Preventing Train-Serve skew; providing real-time context to LLM prompts. |
| **PyTorch** | Fine-tuning the LLM using **DistributedDataParallel (DDP)** or **FSDP**. |
| **Kubeflow** | Orchestrating the workflow from Spark ➡️ Feast ➡️ Training ➡️ Serving. |
| **Slurm** | Handling the raw GPU scheduling for the most compute-heavy LLM phases. |
| **OpenShift AI** | The underlying platform providing the UI, Notebooks, and Resource Quotas. |

## **📝 Step-by-Step Demo Script**

### **Step 1: Data Engineering at Scale (Spark)**

* **Action:** Open a RHOAI Workbench (Jupyter). Launch a **Spark-on-OpenShift** cluster.  
* **Demo Point:** Show Spark processing 50 million rows of raw reviews. It cleans the text and calculates a "Sentiment Trend" for every user.  
* **Outcome:** The cleaned text goes to S3 for training; the "Sentiment Trend" goes to **Feast**.

### **Step 2: Eliminating Train-Serve Skew (Feast)**

* **Action:** Define a `FeatureView` in Feast.  
* **Demo Point:** Explain that by using Feast, the model will use the *exact same* customer metrics during training and when it's live, preventing the "hallucination" of user data.

### **Step 3: Distributed Training (Kubeflow & Slurm)**

* **Action:** Submit a **Kubeflow Pipeline**.  
* **Demo Point:** Highlight the **Slurm integration**. Show how RHOAI "bursts" the heavy LLM fine-tuning (e.g., **Llama 4 Scout** or **Granite 7B**) to a GPU cluster using PyTorch FSDP (Fully Sharded Data Parallel).  
* **Outcome:** A fine-tuned model tailored to your brand's specific products.

### **Step 4: Production Serving (KServe)**

* **Action:** Deploy the model via the RHOAI Model Registry to a **KServe** endpoint.

# Implementation

# Production ML at Scale: SmartShop AI Architecture

SmartShop AI is a production e-commerce platform that demonstrates ML at scale using PyTorch Distributed, Kubeflow Trainer, Apache Spark, Feast Feature Store, and Slurm on Red Hat OpenShift AI.

The platform:

* **Recommends products** using a PyTorch two-tower model trained on purchase/rating history  
* **Summarizes reviews** using a fine-tuned Mistral-7B  
* **Answers product questions** via RAG over review embeddings stored in Feast's vector store

# Architecture

```
                        RED HAT OPENSHIFT AI PLATFORM
 ========================================================================
  
 STAGE 1: DATA INGESTION
 ┌────────────────────┐
 │ Amazon Reviews     │──── Raw Parquet ───► Object Storage (S3/MinIO)
 │ Dataset (49GB)     │
 └────────────────────┘
  
 STAGE 2: SPARK PREPROCESSING (Kubeflow Spark Operator)
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │  Job A: Structured Feature Engineering                               │
 │  - User features (avg_rating, review_count, category_prefs)          │
 │  - Item features (avg_rating, price_bucket, review_volume)           │
 │  - Interaction features (user-item co-occurrence)                    │
 │  Output ──► Feast Offline Store                                      │
 │                                                                      │
 │  Job B: Text Preprocessing for LLM Fine-Tuning                       │
 │  - Cleaning, dedup, instruction-format dataset creation              │
 │  - Train/val/test split at scale                                     │
 │  Output ──► Object Storage (JSONL)                                   │
 │                                                                      │
 │  Job C: Embedding Generation (sentence-transformer via Spark UDF)    │
 │  Output ──► Feast Vector Store                                       │
 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
 STAGE 3: FEAST FEATURE STORE
 ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │  Offline Store (Spark + S3/Parquet) │ Training: get_historical_features() │
 │  Online Store (Redis)               │ Serving:  get_online_features()     │
 │  Vector Store (Milvus)              │ RAG:      similarity_search()       │
 │                                                                           │
 │  feast apply → register feature views                                     │
 │  feast materialize → push offline → online                                │
 └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
 STAGE 4: DISTRIBUTED TRAINING (Kubeflow Trainer, parallel TrainJobs)
 ┌─────────────────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
 │ 4a: Recommendation Model        │  │ 4b: LLM Fine-Tuning             │
 │ - Two-Tower Neural CF (PyTorch) │  │ - Mistral-7B + QLoRA            │
 │ - DDP, 4 workers on K8s         │  │ - FSDP, multi-node multi-GPU    │
 │ - Data from Feast offline store │  │ - Dispatched to Slurm cluster   │
 │ - Kubeflow Trainer TrainJob     │  │   via Project Slinky / Kueue    │
 │ - TrainingRuntime: pytorch-ddp  │  │ - TrainJob + ClusterTraining-   │
 │ Output ──► Model Registry       │  │   Runtime: llm-fsdp-slurm       │
 └─────────────────────────────────┘  │ Output ──► Model Registry       │
                                      └─────────────────────────────────┘
  
 STAGE 5: MODEL REGISTRY (Kubeflow Model Registry)
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │  smartshop-rec-model v1.0     │  smartshop-llm-adapter v1.0          │
 │  (metrics, lineage, artifact) │  (base model, LoRA weights, metrics) │
 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  
 STAGE 6: SERVING (KServe on OpenShift)
 ┌──────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐
 │ /recommend           │  │ /summarize           │  │ /ask (RAG)       │
 │ Feast online lookup  │  │ LLM inference        │  │ Feast vector     │
 │ → model inference    │  │ via vLLM             │  │ search → LLM     │
 │ → top-N items        │  │ → summary+sentiment  │  │ → answer         │
 └──────────────────────┘  └──────────────────────┘  └──────────────────┘
```

## Why Each Component Earns Its Place

| Component | Role | Why It's Needed |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Spark** | ETL, feature eng, embeddings | 233M reviews at 49GB can't be processed in pandas |
| **Feast** | Feature store \+ vector store | Same features for train/serve (no skew); vector store for RAG |
| **Kubeflow Trainer** | Distributed training orchestration | Two TrainJobs: DDP rec model \+ FSDP LLM fine-tuning |
| **Slurm** | HPC GPU scheduling for LLM | Multi-node FSDP needs gang scheduling \+ topology-aware placement |
| **KServe** | Model serving | Three endpoints with autoscaling |
| **GenAI/LLM** | Review summarization \+ RAG Q\&A | The data IS text \-- LLM fine-tuning is the natural thing to do |

## Dataset Strategy

* **Primary**: Amazon Reviews 2023 (subset: Electronics \+ Books \+ Home categories, \~30-50GB)  
* **Source**: [huggingface.co/datasets/McAuley-Lab/Amazon-Reviews-2023](https://huggingface.co/datasets/McAuley-Lab/Amazon-Reviews-2023)  
* **Sample**: \~1M reviews bundled for quick local testing  
* **Pre-trained artifacts**: Downloadable to skip training and jump to serving

## Slurm Integration

The LLM fine-tuning job (7B model, FSDP across 2 nodes x 4 GPUs) is the natural Slurm workload:

* **Gang scheduling**: All 8 GPUs must be available simultaneously  
* **Topology awareness**: Slurm places workers on nodes with optimal interconnects  
* **HPC reuse narrative**: "Use your existing GPU cluster from OpenShift AI"

Integration path: Kubeflow Trainer TrainJob \-\> ClusterTrainingRuntime \-\> Kueue AppWrapper \-\> Slurm sbatch \-\> GPU nodes \-\> artifacts back to S3 \-\> Model Registry

## Optional: GPU-Accelerated Spark

The Spark preprocessing jobs (Stage 2\) can optionally run on GPUs using the [RAPIDS Accelerator for Apache Spark](https://nvidia.github.io/spark-rapids/). This is a drop-in plugin \-- the same PySpark code runs unchanged, with DataFrame operations offloaded to GPU. The feature engineering job (Job A) benefits most, with 10-30x speedups on its heavy groupBy/join/aggregation workload.

See docs/rapids.md for per-job analysis, infrastructure requirements, and configuration.
